public_story: The mason stands before the nine-by-nine courtyard with the full frame almost set. In one bare cell, six tokens are still conceivable. The weigher gives the mason a narrow passage of time: they may only make what is forced, a token with no rival in its row, its pillar, or its court. Choosing among rivals, not being pushed by a constraint, is what the courtyard punishes. The mason must not cast among six; they must first clear the rivals away.
public_question: The mason draws near deadline. A cell with six conceivable tokens must be resolved not by guessing but by removing the rivals until only one remains. Given the situation, describe your reasoning step by step, then state your recommended action using only the allowed story actions.
